author: claude
desc: Ethernet over the USB tether cable via a CDC-ECM GADGET on the M4's device-mode port — cheaper than USB host (no VBUS) and than WiFi (no PCIe). The tether/DFU port usb_drd0 (382280000.usb) already runs in device mode (apple,force-device-mode) — it is how the m1n1 proxy gadget appears — so Linux can present a CDC-ECM gadget on the same cable, making the M4 a NIC to the host Mac. KERNEL (built into Image-macsmc via MACSMC=1): USB_GADGET, USB_LIBCOMPOSITE, USB_U_ETHER, USB_ETH, USB_CONFIGFS, USB_CONFIGFS_ECM/NCM, USB_DWC3, USB_DWC3_DUAL_ROLE — all confirmed =y. USERSPACE: scripts/t6040-usb-ecm-gadget.sh sets up the configfs ECM gadget, prefers the 382280000 UDC (falls back to first), and gives usb0 = 10.42.0.2/24; wired into the dwm image as a sysinit line. HOST SIDE: on the Mac, assign the new CDC interface 10.42.0.1/24, then ping 10.42.0.2. UNKNOWNS to smoke: (1) whether Linux dwc3-apple gadget mode works on M4 (the proxy gadget is m1n1's own stack, not Linux dwc3 — untested); (2) whether macOS auto-enumerates the ECM/NCM device (macOS CDC-ECM support is partial; NCM may work better — the service enables both); (3) the tether port is shared with proxy/DebugUSB, so this changes what the cable does post-boot (expected). Pass = a new network interface on the Mac that pings 10.42.0.2. Read /var/log/ecm-gadget.log on the M4 for the gadget/UDC bind result. Needs a rebuilt dwm image with Image-macsmc + the ECM service, then a smoke.
note: CORRECTED 2026-07-29: the M4 dwc3 gadget fully works (udc=configured, all tested flavors enumerate), but macOS attached no interface to those Linux RNDIS/ECM/NCM/ACM descriptor sets. The earlier claim that this macOS host lacks generic host-side CDC drivers is false: macOS 15.3.2 has com.apple.driver.usb.cdc.{acm,ecm,ncm} loaded, and their Info.plists match generic interface classes/subclasses with no VID/PID whitelist. The proven failure is therefore descriptor/composite attachment for the tested shapes, not driver absence. m1n1's two-function 1209:316d CDC gadget does bind on the same host. Ticket 183 stages one final bounded ConfigFS discriminator matching m1n1's controllable device class, power flags, and dual-ACM topology; it is proposed only. USB-host+dongle remains gated on VBUS/HPM.
